# Video script and shot list (DRAFT) > **DRAFT:** written from the design docs and decision log before Dinakar's rationale interview. > Update the talking points with his answers from `docs/design-rationale.md` before recording. > The bullets are talking points, not lines to read. Say them in your own words. **Target:** about 7:00, hard cap 8:00. **Format:** a screenshare with voice (face cam optional). **Shape:** show first, explain after. The demo takes about half the time, and the brief's seven points are woven in (marked **[B1]–[B7]**). Brief points: **B1** option and why · **B2** design/prototyping process · **B3** enhances, not replaces, agency · **B4** learning principles · **B5** measuring success · **B6** scaling to millions · **B7** sister-team adoption. ## Timed segments | Time | Screen / shot | Talking points | |---|---|---| | **0:00–0:30** Hook **[B1]** | Landing page, fresh tab (Tab 0). Type `/co-learn` and let the unlock animation and sound play. | • "I picked Option B: learning *through* AI-assisted work."
• The problem: Claude can do the work for you, so people get results without growing. Co-learn keeps the work and adds the growth.
• It's imagined as a mode you switch on inside Claude, which is why the entry is a slash command. | | **0:30–0:50** Intent | Tab 0: the intent screen, with the mode switch (Work on something / Learn a topic), "What are you working on?", and "Try the demo: train a churn model". Click through familiarity and time. | • The target user is a working professional in an area they aren't expert in, e.g. a PM training a churn model.
• At most three quick questions, then the work starts right away (the goal becomes the first message). | | **0:50–1:50** A real fork **[B3][B4]** | **Tab A** (Co-learn churn session paused at a *Decide* question: "which metric?"). Scroll up briefly to show real code and output, then the question card. Type a free-form answer (e.g. "recall, because missing a churner costs more"), submit, and show the "why" and XP. | • Claude is really running Python (Anthropic's code execution tool): real metrics, not simulated.
• Questions land at the **real fork**: Claude did everything that didn't depend on my answer first (P10, protect the flow).
• **Agency:** my answer steers the work. Claude builds the pipeline around *my* metric, and if I pick a weak but safe option it follows it and lets the results show why.
• Free recall first, multiple choice only if I struggle; every answer gets a short "why" (P3, Kornell/Hays/Bjork). | | **1:50–2:30** Help without handing over the answer **[B3][B4]** | **Tab B** (an open question card). Open "Give me a hint", then "Help me learn this" → "Ask Claude…" and type "just tell me". Show the kind decline. | • Being stuck shouldn't be a dead end: a hint ladder, "Teach me" (a worked similar example), and a chat inside the card.
• Claude won't give the answer before you've tried (retrieval practice). It declines once; ask again and it reveals, with no credit and the concept marked for review.
• Help reduces XP and mastery credit but XP never goes negative: honest signal, no punishment (P2). | | **2:30–3:10** Boss **[B4]** | **Tab C** (boss offer showing, "Take it on, about 2 min / Keep working"). Click *Take it on*, answer one question, show the hit, the ASCII boss and the sound. | • When a chunk of work finishes, a boss recombines the recent concepts (cumulative practice).
• It's opt-in, and "Keep working" never blocks the work.
• Rewards scale with the milestone: small sound → jingle → boss win with confetti (P2, it feels like a game). | | **3:10–3:45** Wrap-up | **Tab D** (a finished session). Click "See the wrap-up": Codex of concepts, "Review next time", XP/level, "Learn more" readings, "Next time you could…". | • You leave with a record: what you learned, what to review (it resurfaces in the next session), and real readings with links.
• Sources everywhere Claude explains a concept, so learners can verify (P9, trustworthy content). | | **3:45–4:20** Learn mode coda **[B1]** | **Tab E** (`/learn`, Roman Republic): path card at the top, a cited lesson, a question after it, a story chapter. | • The same engine generalizes to pure topic learning: a 3-part path, ~120-word cited lessons, a question after each, bosses as chapter tests.
• Story chapters live *here*, not in Co-learn. Playtesting showed a story competed with real work, so I cut it there (a design call driven by testing). | | **4:20–5:05** Process **[B2]** | Repo on GitHub: `docs/design-principles.md`, then `docs/decision-log.md` (scroll). Optionally `docs/design-plan.md`. | • Principles first, before choosing the option, so the option was chosen for learning reasons.
• Research-backed decisions (challenge bands, code execution) and a decision log with alternatives for each.
• Built with Claude Code: I owned the decisions, Claude proposed options. Contracts-first parallel tracks.
• Playtest → change: story removed, questions moved to the real fork, help tools added. *(Pick 1–2 examples from your rationale.)* | | **5:05–5:40** Principles recap **[B4]** | Back to the app: Settings (gear) → guardrails Light/Balanced/Strict. | • "Code paces, Claude creates" (P8): a small deterministic engine decides *when* and *how hard*; Claude writes, grades and works. Predictable and testable.
• Targets about 80% correct (85–90% for new concepts, 65–80% for bosses); back off fast after misses.
• No quota by default: a quality bar decides; opt-in guardrails for fewer interruptions. | | **5:40–6:15** Measuring success **[B5]** | `/insights` (Settings → "How Co-learn is doing"). Point at the answer/skip rates, P5 band adherence, delayed retention, and the 👍 rate. | • Success means people **still finish their work** *and* **remember later**: delayed retention on resurfaced concepts is the headline number, not XP.
• Watch skip/defer rates for over-interruption and band adherence for difficulty.
• Early signal: questions were landing above the band (too easy), which is a tuning input.
• Next: A/B the guardrail defaults. | | **6:15–6:40** Scaling **[B6]** | Stay on `/insights`, or show `web/lib/engine/` in the repo. | • Stateless serverless routes, small per-user state, prompt caching, cheap models for grading/hints, the engine costs nothing.
• About $0.20–0.30 per 10-minute session today, with spend caps and rate limits.
• For launch: real accounts, tune defaults from data, compaction for long sessions (already in). | | **6:40–7:05** Sister-team adoption **[B7]** | `web/lib/contracts/` in the repo (the `learning_moment` tool and `EngineApi`). | • The reusable piece is a **tool contract + pacing engine**: any surface (Claude Code as `/co-learn`, Claude.ai as a toggle) adds the tool and renders the card.
• A shared mastery profile follows the user across surfaces; the same events give them `/insights` out of the box.
• Future: a local bridge so moments run inside your own Claude Code session. | | **7:05–7:20** Close | Back to the landing page. | • One line: Claude does the work *with* you, and you come out more capable.
• Thanks. | ## Pre-staged tabs (all test mode: open with `?test=1`) Open each in its own tab before recording so you never wait on Claude on camera (lessons take 14–24s, code runs longer). | Tab | URL / start | State it must be in | |---|---|---| | **Tab 0** | `https://anthropic-take-home-10-17-26.vercel.app/?test=1` (fresh, locked). Use "Start over as a new user" if it opens unlocked. | Landing page with the empty `/co-learn` box. | | **Tab A** | Co-learn, "Try the demo: train a churn model", familiarity *Some*, 10 min. | Paused at a **Decide** question (ideally "which metric?") with code output visible above it. Don't answer it. | | **Tab B** | Co-learn churn session (can be a second demo session). | An **unanswered** question card with no help used yet. | | **Tab C** | Co-learn churn session, played through ≥ 3 concepts. | The **boss offer** card showing ("Take it on…"). | | **Tab D** | A Co-learn session played to the end. | Wrapped up: the "See the wrap-up" button, with the Codex, "Learn more" and suggestions present. | | **Tab E** | `/learn` → "the fall of the Roman Republic". | Path card visible, the first lesson with sources, a question below it, and ideally one story chapter. | | **Tab F** | `/insights` with "Include test traffic" **on** (production has little real traffic). | Charts populated. | | **Tab G** | GitHub repo: `docs/decision-log.md`, with `docs/design-principles.md` and `web/lib/contracts/` in further tabs. | Scrolled to the top. | Tabs A–D can come from one or two sessions if you save the URLs (`/s/`) at each state. A reload restores the state. Note: test tabs show a small "Test traffic (this tab)" badge in the corner. It's fine to leave it, or mention it in one breath. ## Recording checklist - [ ] Update the talking points from the finished `docs/design-rationale.md`. - [ ] All tabs above staged and checked (reload each once). - [ ] Browser: one window, zoom 110–125% so the text reads on video; bookmarks bar hidden; notifications off (Focus mode). - [ ] Sound on for the unlock and boss sounds (check the recorder captures system audio, or mention the sounds). - [ ] Recorder: macOS ⌘⇧5 → Record Selected Portion, Options → microphone on (or Loom/QuickTime). 1080p. - [ ] One rehearsal against a timer; cut segments that run over (the process and scaling segments compress best). - [ ] One take is fine, and small stumbles are fine. Stop under 8:00. - [ ] Watch it back once at 1.5×; check the audio is audible all the way through. - [ ] Upload (unlisted YouTube/Loom/Drive link with view access) and put the link in the Greenhouse text. web/app/api/chat: route.test.ts route.ts web/lib/claude: client.ts content models.ts work web/lib/engine: boss.test.ts boss.ts difficulty.test.ts difficulty.ts gate.test.ts gate.ts guardrails.test.ts guardrails.ts index.test.ts index.ts levels.ts mastery.test.ts mastery.ts math.ts review.test.ts review.ts rewards.test.ts state.test.ts state.ts summary.test.ts summary.ts test-helpers.ts xp.ts web/lib/store: conformance.test.ts defaults.ts errors.ts fake-redis.ts fixtures.ts index.ts memory.ts redis-kv.ts redis.live.test.ts redis.test.ts redis.ts testTraffic.test.ts testTraffic.ts (eval):1: no matches found: --include=*.ts (eval):1: no matches found: --include=*.ts
